$comment: Release notes for Settings > Changelog. Newest first — the first entry's version and date are also what the About panel reports. IMPORTANT: the first entry's version must match `version` in apps/desktop/package.json, which is what app.getVersion() returns and what the updater compares against a GitHub release; if the two drift, the About panel reports one version while the update check reasons about another (tests/changelog.test.ts guards this). Each entry: version (semver), date (YYYY-MM-DD), and changes grouped by type. Types: added | changed | fixed | removed. Add the next entry above this one when a version is actually published — not while it is still being built.

changes.text: Library with shelves, custom categories, grid and list views, and filtering
Linked sources — attach other sources' copies of a title, and the reader offers them when a chapter won't load or the next one is missing
Discover — browse and search any source you have installed, with previews before you add a title
Migrate a whole source at once — find matches across sources in your chosen order, check or pick them by hand, and keep the progress running while you browse
Sources are installed from repositories you add yourself, and run sandboxed with no filesystem, environment or direct network access of their own
Source health — see which installed sources are working, which are waiting out a cooldown, and which need updating before they will load
Sources behind a browser check can be opened once in the desktop app, or given a session pasted from your own browser that you can view, edit and delete
Reader with two-page, single page and long strip layouts, configurable preloading, brightness, page gap and reading direction
Long strip scrolling controls — a scroll-speed slider, hands-free auto-scroll with its own speed, and controls that get out of the way as you scroll down
Reader image tools — crop borders, split or rotate wide pages, spreads on their own screen, colour filters, a custom tint, and 2× enhancement for low-resolution pages
Rebindable keys, a shortcut sheet, mouse-wheel page turns, double-click zoom, click-zone layouts and gamepad controls
Guided view, which steps through a page one panel at a time
Translate a Japanese page in place — the text is read on your device and translated through your own LibreTranslate or DeepL
Offline downloads with a per-chapter queue, live progress, and pause and resume
Automatic downloads — download new chapters, read ahead, and delete chapters after reading
Local CBZ collection in the desktop app — import your own comic archives and read them with the same reader as the rest of your library
Local comics also take ZIP, EPUB and folders of images, read ComicInfo.xml, read library folders in place, and open by drag and drop or from .cbz files
Reading history, a recents view, and a notifications centre for new chapters
Library update rules — skip titles with unread chapters or not started, include or exclude categories, per-category intervals, and smart updates by expected release
An Upcoming page with a release calendar
New-chapter alerts outside the app through ntfy, Discord, Telegram or webhooks
Statistics covering read duration, chapter totals and how your library breaks down
Reading goals and a "year in manga" summary you can save as an image
Themes, accent colours, interface density and scale, plus keyboard shortcuts for moving between sections
Designed for phone, tablet and desktop widths alike, with keyboard navigation, visible focus and screen-reader labelling throughout
Optional accounts, with reading state synced between devices — the app works fully without one
Export your library, reading history and preferences at any time, and restore them into a fresh install
Automatic backups on a schedule, restored through the same preview as an imported file
Import a Mihon or Tachiyomi backup, searching your sources by name, in your order, for titles from sources you don't have
Progress tracking against AniList and MyAnimeList for linked titles
More trackers — MangaUpdates, Kitsu, Shikimori and Bangumi, plus self-hosted Komga and Kavita
App-wide incognito mode, which saves no history or progress and sends nothing to trackers
Desktop app — one installer that runs the reader, its API and its database on your machine, and updates itself from GitHub Releases
Desktop app lock with a PIN or password, and hiding the window from screen capture
Self-hosted server — run the reader and its API on your own machine and reach your library from any device, with health checks and a documented backup and upgrade path
